meta.title: The 16 Personality Types
meta.note: Study citations were written from memory of the literature. Verify each before publishing. Percentages and correlations are approximate. Frame results as entertainment and self-reflection, not diagnosis.
meta.us_frequency_source: MBTI Manual (1998) US national sample, approximate

dimensions.description: Concrete facts and present detail vs. patterns and possibilities

dimensions.description: Logic and objective criteria vs. values and impact on people

how_quizzes_work.summary: Each question maps to one dichotomy and one pole. Answers add weighted points to a pole; the higher total wins. Likert items are signed (for example -3..+3) and opposite-pole items are reverse-scored.
how_quizzes_work.pseudo_code: score_D = sum(answer_value * direction * weight); letter = A if score_D > 0 else B; percent_A = 50 + 50 * score_D / max_possible
formats: Forced choice (official MBTI Form M, 93 items)

how_ai_detects.summary: Personality shapes word choice, topics, sentence structure and sentiment. Models learn weak statistical links between text and known types and combine hundreds of cues. Best shown as per-dimension probabilities.
pipeline: Clean and remove explicit type mentions (label leakage)
Evaluate with balanced accuracy and macro-F1

studies.citation: McCrae, R. R., & Costa, P. T. (1989). Reinterpreting the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator from the perspective of the five-factor model of personality. Journal of Personality, 57(1), 17-40.
studies.summary: Showed each MBTI scale maps onto a Big Five trait: E/I with Extraversion, S/N with Openness, T/F with Agreeableness, J/P with Conscientiousness. Argued the scales are continuous, not two-type categories.

studies.citation: Furnham, A. (1996). The big five versus the big four: the relationship between the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator and NEO-PI five factor model of personality. Personality and Individual Differences, 21(2).
studies.summary: Replicated the MBTI-to-Big-Five pattern and noted Neuroticism has no MBTI counterpart.

studies.citation: Pittenger, D. J. (1993). Measuring the MBTI... and coming up short. Journal of Career Planning and Employment, 54(1).
studies.summary: Influential critique of the MBTI's reliability, validity and the either-or typing of continuous traits.

studies.citation: Pittenger, D. J. (2005). Cautionary comments regarding the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator. Consulting Psychology Journal, 57(3).
studies.summary: Updated review of reliability and validity concerns, including how often people change type on retest.

studies.citation: Capraro, R. M., & Capraro, M. M. (2002). Myers-Briggs Type Indicator score reliability across studies: a meta-analytic reliability generalization study. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 62(4).
studies.summary: Meta-analysis suggesting internal consistency of the MBTI scales is generally acceptable.

studies.citation: Boyle, G. J. (1995). Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI): some psychometric limitations. Australian Psychologist, 30(1).
studies.summary: Review of psychometric limitations of the MBTI.

studies.citation: McCarley, N. G., & Carskadon, T. G. (1983). Test-retest reliabilities of scales and subscales of the MBTI and of criterion-keyed Form G for Sensing-Intuition. Journal of Psychological Type.
studies.summary: Early test-retest work often cited for type-change rates over short intervals.

studies.citation: Pennebaker, J. W., & King, L. A. (1999). Linguistic styles: language use as an individual difference. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 77(6).
studies.summary: Showed word-category use (LIWC approach) is stable within people and relates to personality.

studies.citation: Mairesse, F., Walker, M. A., Mehl, M. R., & Moore, R. K. (2007). Using linguistic cues for the automatic recognition of personality in conversation and text. Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research, 30.
studies.summary: Early automatic personality recognition from text and speech.

studies.citation: Yarkoni, T. (2010). Personality in 100,000 words: a large-scale analysis of personality and word use among bloggers. Journal of Research in Personality, 44(3).
studies.summary: Linked Big Five traits to specific word categories in blog text, e.g. Neuroticism with negative emotion words, Extraversion with social words.

studies.citation: Schwartz, H. A., et al. (2013). Personality, gender, and age in the language of social media: the open-vocabulary approach. PLoS ONE, 8(9).
studies.summary: Analyzed Facebook language of about 75,000 volunteers and found interpretable word and topic differences by Big Five trait.

studies.citation: Kosinski, M., Stillwell, D., & Graepel, T. (2013). Private traits and attributes are predictable from digital records of human behavior. PNAS, 110(15).
studies.summary: Predicted personality and other traits from Facebook Likes.

studies.citation: Youyou, W., Kosinski, M., & Stillwell, D. (2015). Computer-based personality judgments are more accurate than those made by humans. PNAS, 112(4).
studies.summary: Found computer judgments from Likes beat judgments by friends and family at certain data sizes.

studies.citation: Matz, S. C., Kosinski, M., Nave, G., & Stillwell, D. J. (2017). Psychological targeting as an effective approach to digital mass persuasion. PNAS, 114(48).
studies.summary: Showed personality-targeted ads can be more effective, which is why transparency and consent matter.

studies.citation: Plank, B., & Hovy, D. (2015). Personality traits on Twitter, or how to get 1,500 personality tests in a week. Workshop on Computational Approaches to Subjectivity, Sentiment and Social Media Analysis.
studies.summary: Trained classifiers on tweets from users who stated their MBTI type; some dimensions were more predictable than others.

studies.citation: Gjurkovic, M., & Snajder, J. (2018). Reddit: a gold mine for personality prediction. Workshop on Computational Modeling of People's Opinions, Personality, and Emotions in Social Media.
studies.summary: Built an MBTI-labelled Reddit dataset and tested prediction from posts.

studies.citation: Gjurkovic, M., et al. (2021). PANDORA talks: personality and demographics on Reddit. Workshop on Natural Language Processing for Computational Social Science.
studies.summary: PANDORA dataset: Reddit users with MBTI, Big Five and Enneagram labels plus demographics.

studies.citation: Rao, H., Leung, C., & Miao, C. (2023). Can ChatGPT assess human personalities? A general evaluation framework. arXiv.
studies.summary: Evaluated whether ChatGPT can assess personality from text; results were meaningful but sensitive to prompt wording.

studies.citation: Serapio-Garcia, G., et al. (2023). Personality traits in large language models. arXiv.
studies.summary: Found larger instruction-tuned LLMs give reliable, valid personality-test answers and that expressed personality can be shaped by prompting.

studies.citation: Jiang, H., et al. (2023). PersonaLLM: investigating the ability of large language models to express personality traits. arXiv.
studies.summary: Persona-prompted LLMs wrote text that reflected the assigned traits.

studies.citation: Peters, H., & Matz, S. C. (2024). Large language models can infer psychological dispositions of social media users. PNAS Nexus.
studies.summary: LLMs inferred Big Five dispositions from social media posts at better-than-chance levels.

types.big_five_tendencies: High Openness and Conscientiousness; lower Extraversion and Agreeableness.
types.summary: Independent long-range strategists who build mental models of systems and look for the most efficient way to improve them.
types.core_characteristics: Driven by competence and vision, hold high standards for self and others, reserved or intense socially.
strengths: Decisiveness once a conclusion is reached
blind_spots: Can seem cold or dismissive of emotion
May undervalue the present moment (inferior Se)
types.relationships_and_communication: Direct, concise, low small talk. Shows loyalty through actions and problem-solving. Prefers few, deep relationships.
types.work_tendencies: Strategy, engineering, research, law, architecture, investing, systems design. Wants autonomy and to be judged on results.
types.under_stress: Inferior Se can appear as impulsive indulgence, sensory overload, or fixating on irrelevant physical details.
types.research_notes: Often studied in leadership and entrepreneurship samples, but results depend on the test. Heavily over-represented in internet datasets relative to its real-world rarity.
ai_detection_signals: Abstract nouns and strategy vocabulary (long-term, framework, optimize, system)

types.work_tendencies: Science, software, mathematics, philosophy, research, game design, data analysis. Wants flexible deadlines and intellectual freedom.
types.under_stress: Inferior Fe can show as oversensitivity to criticism, feeling misunderstood, or sudden emotional outbursts.
types.research_notes: Strongly tied to Openness in MBTI-Big Five studies. Common in online programming and philosophy communities.
ai_detection_signals: Hedged, qualified statements (technically, in theory, it depends)
Interest in systems, logic, science, games

types.relationships_and_communication: Direct, assertive, goal-oriented. Shows care through support, provision and high expectations.

types.under_stress: Inferior Fi can show as hurt feelings they rarely admit, withdrawal, or sudden moral outbursts.
